result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_weighted()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if the graph is weighted. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L5475-L5525){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_weighted() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Is weighted](/assets/graphs/is-weighted.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Left: a triangle whose edges carry the weights 2.5, 4, and 1, a graph created as weighted, so is_weighted() returns True. Right: the same triangle with no weights, so is_weighted() returns False." width="100%"} Returns whether this graph supports edge weights. This property is set when the graph is created and cannot be changed afterward. Weighted graphs can store numeric weights on edges, which are used in algorithms like shortest path, minimum spanning tree, etc. In weighted graphs: - each edge can have an associated numeric weight - weights represent costs, distances, capacities, etc. - algorithms consider weights when computing paths and metrics In unweighted graphs: - all edges are treated equally (implicit weight of `1`) - weights are ignored or unavailable - algorithms use hop count instead of weight sum ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the graph supports weights, `False` otherwise. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#b924d5a8 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec ec.Graph(weighted=True).is_weighted(), ec.Graph().is_weighted() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (True, False) ``` ::: ::: Branching on `is_weighted()` avoids passing a `weight=` that would otherwise be silently ignored: ::: {#bb387cb5 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph(weighted=True).add_node(label="A").add_node(label="B") if graph.is_weighted(): graph.add_edge(source="A", target="B", weight=2.5) else: graph.add_edge(source="A", target="B") graph.get_edge(graph.get_edge_ids()[0]).weight ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 2.5 ``` ::: :::
